Let
\[
I_n(\lambda)=\iint_{(x-1)^2+y^2\le (1+\lambda)^2} e^{-n(x^2+y^2)}\,dx\,dy .
\]
The total Gaussian integral over the plane is \(\pi/n\), so the condition asks that this shifted disk capture exactly half the mass.

Set
\[
x=\frac X{\sqrt n},\qquad y=\frac Y{\sqrt n},\qquad \lambda=\frac tn .
\]
Then
\[
I_n(\lambda)=\frac1n\iint_{\Omega_{n,t}} e^{-(X^2+Y^2)}\,dX\,dY.
\]
Near the origin, the relevant boundary of the disk is the left boundary
\[
x=1-\sqrt{(1+\lambda)^2-y^2}.
\]
Thus in scaled variables,
\[
X_-(Y)=\sqrt n\left(1-\sqrt{(1+t/n)^2-\frac{Y^2}{n}}\right).
\]
Using \(\varepsilon=n^{-1/2}\), expand:
\[
X_-(Y)
=\varepsilon\left(\frac{Y^2}{2}-t\right)
+\varepsilon^3\left(\frac12\left(\frac{Y^2}{2}-t\right)^2-\frac{t^2}{2}\right)
+O(\varepsilon^5(1+|Y|^6)).
\]
The right boundary of the disk is at \(X\sim 2\sqrt n\), so its omitted Gaussian contribution is exponentially small.

Therefore
\[
n I_n(t/n)
=
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-Y^2}
\int_{X_-(Y)}^\infty e^{-X^2}\,dX\,dY+O(e^{-cn}).
\]
For small \(s\),
\[
\int_s^\infty e^{-X^2}\,dX
=\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2}-s+\frac{s^3}{3}+O(s^5).
\]
Let
\[
u(Y)=\frac{Y^2}{2}-t,\qquad
v(Y)=\frac12u(Y)^2-\frac{t^2}{2}.
\]
Then
\[
nI_n(t/n)-\frac\pi2
=
-\varepsilon\int e^{-Y^2}u(Y)\,dY
+\varepsilon^3\left(-\int e^{-Y^2}v(Y)\,dY+\frac13\int e^{-Y^2}u(Y)^3\,dY\right)
+O(\varepsilon^5).
\]

Using
\[
\int e^{-Y^2}\,dY=\sqrt\pi,\qquad
\int Y^2e^{-Y^2}\,dY=\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2},
\]
the first-order term is
\[
-\varepsilon\sqrt\pi\left(\frac14-t\right)
=\varepsilon\sqrt\pi\left(t-\frac14\right).
\]
Hence \(t\to 1/4\), i.e. \(\lambda_n\sim 1/(4n)\).

Now put
\[
t=\frac14+\frac bn+o(n^{-1}).
\]
We need the next coefficient at \(t=1/4\). With the normalized Gaussian moments
\[
\mathbb E[Y^2]=\frac12,\qquad
\mathbb E[Y^4]=\frac34,\qquad
\mathbb E[Y^6]=\frac{15}{8},
\]
at \(t=1/4\) we have
\[
\mathbb E[u^2]=\frac18,\qquad
\mathbb E[u^3]=\frac18,
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E[v]
=\frac12\mathbb E[u^2]-\frac12t^2
=\frac1{16}-\frac1{32}
=\frac1{32}.
\]
Thus the \(\varepsilon^3\)-coefficient equals
\[
-\frac1{32}+\frac13\cdot\frac18
=-\frac1{32}+\frac1{24}
=\frac1{96}.
\]
The equation \(I_n(\lambda_n)=\pi/(2n)\) gives
\[
0=\varepsilon\sqrt\pi\left(t-\frac14\right)
+\varepsilon^3\sqrt\pi\cdot\frac1{96}
+O(\varepsilon^5),
\]
so
\[
t-\frac14=-\frac1{96n}+O(n^{-2}).
\]
Since \(t=n\lambda_n\),
\[
n^2\left(\lambda_n-\frac1{4n}\right)
=n\left(t-\frac14\right)\to -\frac1{96}.
\]

\[
\boxed{-\frac1{96}}
\]
